newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 24.

text.p: Following are the highlights of storiday.

- Concerns have arisen over a repeat of last summer's Drumcree stand-off following a decision by the predominantly loyalist Orange Order not to meet the mostly republican Garvaghy Residents' Coalition to discuss a compromise.
- The British government agreed to adopt a tougher stance against Europe on Thursday and announced it was unlikely that Britain would join a single currency in January 1999.
- Irish people earning over 35,000 a year will again enjoy the same dental and optical benefits as those on lower salaries, the Department of Social Welfare confirmed on Thursday.
- Sterling has suddenly reversed direction on the foreign exchange markets, falling sharply and allowing the Irish Central Bank to push the Irish pound down in the ERM.
- The Irish government has banned any meeting between top officials and republican Sinn Fein unless it first gets "reliable assurances" that an IRA ceasefire will follow quickly.
- A mid-summer mini-Budget to counter inflation is possible in Ireland because of the stimulus in the Irish government's Budget on Wednesday, say Goodbody Stockbrokers.

- Almost six out of every ten small businesses have identified access to skilled employees as a factor which limits the growth of their companies, a survey of firms in the south-east of Ireland has revealed.
